claims.text: Aitchison’s colonial account names Sanaa’s 1891 governor-general. Aden’s report names a Resident and magistrate. The Bir Ali agreement instead prescribes protection and restricted foreign dealings for named Wahidi dependencies, with later ratification. These are different governing relations, not proof neighboring protection established Aden’s city offices or universal consent.
